div.p: url: Ordering through an order server
version: 1.0.0
name: TaskOrderScenario
title: Ordering through an order server
status: Active
experimental: true
publisher: José Costa Teixeira
contact: José Costa Teixeira: https://github.com/costateixeira, José Costa Teixeira: you-know.it@gmail.com
description:
A placer puts an order and a Task on an order server. The unit polls the server, dispenses what is addressed to it, and reports back what it did.
jurisdiction: World
purpose:
The long way round, and the one that behaves like a real workflow.

An order on a server is an authorization: it says a chocolate may be dispensed, not that one should be dispensed now. Something else has to ask for it to be fulfilled. A Task is that something, and Task.requestedPerformer is the only place in R5 that can name the Device meant to do the work.
The unit is never connected to from outside here. It polls, which is what lets a dispenser sit on a conference network with nothing open to it.
Creates the order and the Task, and closes the order once the Task is done. A Task closes itself; a MedicationRequest does not.
A plain FHIR server. It holds the order and the Task until a unit collects them, and it has to answer _include=Task:focus.
Acting here as a FHIR client. It takes only the work addressed to it and leaves everything else alone.
An untagged MedicationRequest, naming the unit meant to fill it in the dispensingDevice extension. On its own it sits there.

blockquote.p: content: MedicationRequest : extension = ->Spenser-E3D4; status = active; intent = instance-order

div.p: As created: authorized, and not yet filled.

blockquote.p: content: MedicationRequest : extension = ->Spenser-E3D4; status = active; intent = instance-order

div.p: After the placer closes it. The unit does not touch the order while a Task is coordinating the work.
A fulfill Task whose focus is the order and whose requestedPerformer is the unit. This is what makes the order actionable.

blockquote.p: content: Task Fulfill the focal request

div.p: As created. Every other unit polling the same server skips it.

blockquote.p: content: Task Fulfill the focal request

div.p: After the chocolate came out, with the dispense in Task.output.
What the unit writes back, naming itself as performer and the order in authorizingPrescription.

blockquote.p: title: Order a chocolate through an order server

div.p: Place the work, let the unit find it, and read back what it did.
The unit has been pointed at the order server and its polling is on. The unit has written its own Device on the server, so a Task can name it.
A chocolate has been dispensed, the dispense is on the server, the Task is completed, and the order is closed.
Nothing happens yet, and that is the point.
code is fulfill, focus is the order, requestedPerformer is the unit. Leave requestedPerformer out and any unit polling that server may take it.

tr.td: Tag the order instead of creating a Task

div.p: Put actionable from common-tags in the order's meta.tag and skip the Task. A unit accepts both routes on every check, and orderMode narrows it to one. With no Task coordinating the work the unit completes the MedicationRequest itself, and step 6 does not happen.

GET /Task?status=requested&_include=Task:focus&_count=5. The unit polls on a timer, and a check can also be asked for by hand. Each check looks at the first five results only, so a long queue on the server can outrun one check. The unit remembers what it has already dealt with.
The servo turns and a piece drops out, and then the unit says so. The write is queued and retried, so a server that was briefly unreachable does not cost the record.

The unit writes a dispense with status of declined and notPerformedReason.concept of outofstock. Whether the Task is then left open, so a refill retries it, or closed as failed, is the unit's keepOrders setting.
PUT /Task/\<id>: status becomes completed, with the dispense in Task.output. Sent with If-Match, so a Task somebody else has moved on is not overwritten.
PUT /MedicationRequest/\<id>. The placer closes its own order. The unit does not: it was asked to fill one Task, and it has no way of knowing whether the order authorized more than that.
